items.title: ‘Landmark’ building demolished to make way for condos in Mississauga
items.summary: A Mississauga business that operated in the south end of the city for more than 100 years closed its doors for good late last year. This week, construction crews began tearing down the two-storey Port Credit building that since 1924 had housed the Skinner & Middlebrook Funeral Home. The local business, which was located on the north side of Lakeshore Road East, at Ann Street just west of Hurontario Street, ceased operations on Sept. 30, 2025. A post on Facebook group Port Credit Life on Thursday read, “Sadly, another landmark gone. ” The post, which included a short video of construction crews demolishing the building late this week, prompted numerous comments from residents. “So very sad,” wrote one commenter, who noted that several generations of their family — parents, grandparents and great-grandparents — had been cared for by Skinner & Middlebrook Funeral Home. ” Skinner & Middlebrook Funeral Home as it appeared over the years.

items.title: Brr-ing on the cold: Get your home winter-ready with these fall maintenance tips
items.summary: As winter rolls in, it can bring some risks to your property. Taking time to inspect your home and yard can help protect against weather-related damage. As Mississauga trades summer sunshine for sweater weather, falling leaves and crisp autumn days, now is the time to prepare for what comes next: winter. Before colder temperatures set in, take time to inspect and clean your property to help protect against weather-related challenges. Being proactive before temperatures drop can help prevent costly damage from colder conditions. This critical upkeep acts as a preventive measure to protect against fire damage (from heating sources), water damage (from frozen pipes) and structural damage (from wind, ice and snow buildup), while helping ensure your home and property are well maintained. Start by winterizing your home and yard. Here are a few ways to protect your property and keep it safe, warm and comfortable through the winter months. Help protect your home from winter weather by ensuring eavestroughs and downspouts are free of leaves, pine needles, sticks and other debris. Keeping them clear ensures proper drainage and helps prevent leaks and water damage. Consider disconnecting roof downspouts from pipes connected to your basement weepers, which help drain water away from your foundation. Instead, direct the runoff onto your lawn or garden using an elbow and downspout extension, ensuring water drains at least three feet away from your home’s foundation. Pruning trees and hedges before winter promotes healthy spring growth, helps prevent damage from heavy snowfall and improves the appearance of your landscape. Storing rain barrels and turning off outdoor faucets helps conserve water, prevent flooding and protect plumbing from freezing.

items.title: Data breach leads to tip line program suspension in Mississauga and Brampton
items.summary: Police in Mississauga and Brampton are suspending a partnership with Crime Stoppers following a massive data breach of the tip line system. Back in March, the “P3” tip software owned by Navigate360 and used by Crime Stoppers was hacked. 5 million tips submitted to Canadian Crime Stoppers programs over the last 25 years were exposed in a data breach, according to reports. ” “The safety and security of Peel residents who have used the Crime Stoppers program is our primary concern. We have requested information from the third-party vendor, Navigate360, to assess any potential risks arising from this breach,” Peel police said in a release. The move by Peel police follows similar steps taken by the Toronto Police Service and the Durham Regional Police Service. A total of 176,859 Toronto tips from January 2022 to November 2025 were in the stolen data, including some 14,973 names. Toronto Crime Stoppers said it is unclear whether those names belong to people who submitted tips, to people named in tips, or both. Peel police say members of the public who wish to provide information about a crime or public safety concern are encouraged to contact officers directly. “While this does not provide the anonymity associated with the Crime Stoppers program, it will ensure information is received directly by investigators,” Peel police said.

items.title: Mississauga's mayoral race a close three-way contest with Bonnie Crombie pulling ahead, a new poll shows
items.summary: The Mississauga mayoral race is one to watch on election night, with a narrow three-way race between the front-runners. From left, incumbent mayor Carolyn Parrish, former mayor Bonnie Crombie and current councillor Alvin Tedjo, are in an epic battle for the top job in Mississauga. Heading into Monday’s municipal election, Mississauga’s mayoral race remains a close three-way race, with former mayor Bonnie Crombie pulling ahead of incumbent mayor Carolyn Parrish, according to a new poll from Liaison Strategies. Meanwhile, current councillor Alvin Tedjo has moved from third place to second, past Parrish, as his campaign lauds the momentum of the “teal wave” in reference to his election sign colour. When accounting for undecided voters, Crombie was at 27 per cent, Tedjo at 24 per cent and Parrish at 21 per cent with 24 per cent undecided. Among decided and leaning voters, Crombie was at 35 per cent, Tedjo at 31 per cent and Parrish at 28 per cent. Liaison Strategies principal David Valentin cautions that the poll is a snapshot in time, done between Oct. 1 percentage points either way. The four candidates discussed housing, property taxes and the “blight” of rogue e-bikes before a crowd in Port Credit Thursday night. items.title: Most expensive home sets sales record in Mississauga
items.summary: A luxurious private estate that just changed hands has officially broken the record for the most expensive home sold not just in Mississauga, but across the entire Region of Peel. Today, Sam McDadi Real Estate Brokerage announced it broke its own record with the city and region’s highest residential sale in history. 1 million, which was set at the Saint George Mansion (2275 Doulton Drive). “It’s been off-market for several months and I had an internal buyer who was quite interested, and we ended up getting two offers,” Sam McDadi told INSAUGA Canada. “It set a record for pricing that’s similar to the Bridal Path, which is great for our city,” he added, referring to the ultra-affluent Toronto neighbourhood that’s famously home to Drake and other well-known Canadian artists and moguls. Following on the heels of the Saint George Mansion, the multi-million-dollar sale is, McDadi says, a sign that Mississauga is a city that luxury homebuilders and buyers should pay attention to. ’’ While McDadi’s team says the exact price and address aren’t being revealed at this time, McDadi can share that the property, massive in size and full of rare amenities, has a special feel. “The architectural design and layout are fantastic. When you walk in there, you realize you have a special property,” he says, adding that the house is relatively new and was custom-built with top-notch touches.

items.title: Freezing property taxes for seniors? Why this would-be Mississauga mayor’s pitch is stirring generational tension
items.summary: Alvin Tedjo’s proposal to freeze Mississauga property taxes for seniors sparks a debate over intergenerational fairness. Dipika Damerla and Alvin Tedjo spar at a mayoral debate at the Mississauga Civic Centre earlier this month. ” A tax break for seniors or fuel for intergenerational warfare? In a municipal election where affordability and rising property taxes are a top concern, a proposal from Mississauga mayoral candidate Alvin Tedjo to permanently “freeze” property tax increases for seniors has opponents claiming working families struggling under hefty mortgages will have to pick up the tab to keep city services running. C. program cited as inspiration by Tedjo has come under fire for benefiting seniors who don’t need the assistance, with reforms becoming a provincial election issue. Tedjo has said that his program would find the right balance to help cash-poor seniors stay in their homes and not burden young property taxpayers, noting that he has a young family himself. One of his mayoral race opponents, Dipika Damerla said Tedjo’s proposal is misleading and could contribute to “intergenerational unfairness” if the program isn’t targeted specifically to low-income seniors. Mississauga is facing what might be its closest mayoral race in a very long time.
